name: Always send Do Not Track from Edge
summary: Edge tells every site that asks that you do not want to be tracked.
what: Applies the Edge policy Configure Do Not Track with the value to always send the request to sites that ask for tracking information. Edge does not send it by default.
benefit: Every site that asks gets your request not to be tracked.
risk: None. It is only a request, and a site decides whether to honor it. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Optional. It costs nothing, but it does not stop a site that ignores it.
facts: Edge does not send Do Not Track unless this is set or the user turns it on
Sites decide whether to honor the request

name: Stop Edge fetching feature assets from Microsoft
summary: Edge features can no longer download their files from the Asset Delivery Service.
what: Applies the Edge policy that disables the Asset Delivery Service. Microsoft describes it as a delivery pipeline whose payloads can be configuration files or machine learning models for Edge features.
benefit: Edge stops fetching those files for its features in the background.
risk: Low. Microsoft says features that depend on the service cannot download what they need to run correctly, so some Edge features may stop working.
advice: Only if you want Edge to fetch as little as possible and can live with some Edge features not working. Revert if a feature stops working.
facts: Microsoft says features that use the service need the downloads to run correctly
